title: Most friends, or the right friends?
hook: Hana has the bigger circle of friends. Bo knows people in two groups. Who matters more?

knows: that some people know more people than others
doesNotKnow: that the person who links groups that don't know each other can matter more than the person with the most friends

misconception: The best-connected person is whoever has the most friends.
objective: The learner can explain that Bo, with fewer friends than Hana, lies on every shortest path between the two groups because his friends include strangers to each other, while Hana's friends all know each other and never need her.

claims.text: On the stage Hana has 5 friends who all know each other (0 pairs of strangers); Bo has 4 friends, and 4 pairs of them are strangers.
claims.source: Stage graph from brief 6 (company/domains/briefs/math.discrete.md, Course: NCM): complete group of 6 (Hana and 5 friends), complete group of 4, Bo linked to 2 of Hana's friends and 2 of the other group. strangerPairs() in Demo.tsx; builder re-run in node 2026-10-14.

claims.text: Every shortest path between someone in Hana's group and someone in the other group runs through Bo: all 24 such pairs. Hana lies on the shortest paths of 0 pairs.
claims.source: BFS shortest-path counts in Demo.tsx (CROSS_VIA_BO = 24; BETWEENNESS[Hana] = 0); builder re-run in node 2026-10-14: betweenness 0,10,10,0,0,0,7,7,0,0,24 for Hana, her friends 1-5, the other group 6-9, Bo.

claims.text: The two people with the most friends on the stage (6 each, Bo's friends in Hana's group) score 10 on the same count, because each carries half the shortest paths that the other could also carry.
claims.source: Betweenness (sum over pairs of the share of shortest paths through the person) in Demo.tsx: 4 group members x 5 people beyond = 20 pairs, each with two equal shortest paths, half each = 10. Degrees 5,6,6,5,5,5,4,4,3,3,4.

claims.text: A person whose friends are not linked to each other spans a gap called a structural hole, and sitting in one can matter more than having the most friends.
claims.source: R. S. Burt, Structural Holes: The Social Structure of Competition, Harvard University Press (1992); Easley and Kleinberg (2010) ch. 3. Attribution: fact-checker confirms (flag carried from the brief).

recall.question: Ana has 30 contacts who all work on one team. Raj has 8 contacts spread over three teams that never talk to each other. Whose departure would cut more lines of communication?
options: Ana's, because she has more contacts
Raj's, because he links teams that have no other link
recall.why: Ana's contacts can all reach each other without her. Raj is the only route between teams, so every message between them goes through him.
